sections.title: The letter name gyé
paragraphs: You call this letter (gyé) /ɟeː/. Its main sound is heard in (gyerek) /ˈɟɛrɛk/, which means child. This letter has only one sound. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. This consonant is always voiced.

sections.title: Making the sound
paragraphs: Press the middle of your tongue flat against the hard roof of your mouth. Keep the tongue tip low behind your bottom teeth. Stop the air completely, then release it smoothly with voice. Voiced means your voice is on. Put your hand on your throat to feel it shake. The sound is a palatal plosive. A plosive stops the air and bursts out.

sections.title: Reading this letter
paragraphs: This letter always makes the same sound in every position. You hear it at the start of a word in (gyerek) /ˈɟɛrɛk/. You also hear it at the end of a word in (ágy) /aːɟ/. Never divide the two written parts when you speak.

sections.title: Avoiding English pitfalls
paragraphs: Do not say the j sound in jam. Jam is an affricate made further forward in the mouth. Do not make two sounds like d followed by y in duty. Keep the tongue flat on the roof of your mouth to make one single smooth sound.
